newsitem.title: GERMANY: Veba Oil sees further profit rise by 2000. [CORRECTED 16:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Veba Oil sees further profit rise by 2000. [CORRECTED 16:40 GMT]

text.p: Veba Oil, a unit of Germany's fourth-biggest company Veba AG, said on Wednesday it sees profitability increasing further for the rest of the century.
"By the year 2000 we will achieve an 800 million mark ($529.3 million) improvement in profits compared to 1994," Veba Oil Board Chairman Wilhelm Bonse-Geuking told journalists at a news conference.

The group said that 300 million of the planned 800 million profit hike would come in the current year, adding that much of the increased profitability was value-added from its refinery and petrochemical business.
Veba Oil also said that it hopes to bring its loss-making mineral oil refinery business back into the black by the start of next year.

The board expects increases in sales and revenues in 1996 and "strongly positive" group profits, which should be along the lines of the 1994 figures, despite the overall weakness of the petrochemical industry.

The company forecast an increase in sales (corrects from profits) to 17 billion marks in full-year 1996, up from 16.3 billion in 1995, while output of mineral oil products in 1996 should hit 20 million tonnes, compared to 19.4 million tonnes in 1995, Veba Oil said.
Veba Oil said the half-year profits were positive, but less than the previous year's figure, although the board would not detail concrete figures.
In 1995 Veba Oil's pre-tax profits increased more than 200 million marks to 427 million marks. ($ = 1.511 German Marks)
